specifications.purpose: Produce an evidence-disciplined diagnosis of a supplied software defect while avoiding premature root-cause and fix claims.

required: Expected behavior or an explicit statement that it is unknown
Observed behavior
At least one evidence item or an explicit statement that evidence is unavailable
invalid_or_blocking_states: No observable failure is described
Supplied evidence is inaccessible or internally contradictory enough to prevent a responsible diagnosis
input_contract.missing_information_behavior: Return DIAGNOSE_FIRST and request only the smallest evidence set with clear diagnostic value.

output_contract.completion_rule: No root cause or fix may be presented as established unless the supplied evidence justifies it; otherwise the result remains diagnostic.

constraints: Use OBSERVED, INFERRED, UNKNOWN, and DISPROVED without promotion
Generate at most five mechanically distinct hypotheses
Rank hypotheses by evidence rather than familiarity
Prefer reversible high-information checks over broad or destructive changes
Never invent runtime state, logs, versions, reproduction results, or infrastructure facts
Separate diagnosis, mitigation, durable fix, and verification

expected_value.statement: Reduce premature fixes and make the next debugging action more discriminating, inspectable, and production-safe.

known_limitations: Cannot observe the runtime or execute checks unless evidence or tools are separately supplied
Quality depends on the completeness and correctness of supplied evidence
One successful fix attempt does not prove root cause
No F4 behavioral, comparative, certification, or portability evidence exists
out_of_scope: Replacing domain-owner judgment for high-impact remediation
acceptance_conditions: Every observation maps to supplied evidence
Hypotheses expose supporting, contradicting, and missing evidence
Checks state true and false expected results plus reversibility
Recommendation status follows the evidence state
Verification covers reproduction, targeted test, regression, and relevant monitoring where applicable

specifications.purpose: Review supplied software changes for material, evidence-backed defects and engineering risks without padding the result with invented findings or style preferences.

required: Code, diff, or exact changed files
Change intent
Runtime or language context sufficient to interpret the change
optional: Performance, security, compatibility, or delivery constraints
Related API, schema, authorization, retry, or external-service contracts
invalid_or_blocking_states: No reviewable code or diff is supplied
Missing context can materially reverse the highest-risk assessment
input_contract.missing_information_behavior: Return REVIEW, avoid invented defects, and identify the minimum additional material required.

output_contract.completion_rule: Every reported finding must include evidence level, location, failure mechanism, impact, smallest useful fix, and verification.

constraints: Report only CONFIRMED, LIKELY, or QUESTION with the level preserved
Tie every finding to the smallest useful code location or snippet
Do not report style preference as a defect
Do not claim tests passed without supplied evidence
Do not call a risky pattern a vulnerability without a reachable threat or missing control
Prioritize material correctness, security, data, reliability, performance, operability, and maintenance risk

expected_value.statement: Concentrate reviewer attention on a small set of material, actionable risks and make uncertainty visible.

known_limitations: Cannot execute code, tests, or static analysis unless tools and authority are separately supplied
Incomplete diffs can hide relevant call sites and contracts
Language or framework semantics may be misinterpreted when context is insufficient
No F4 behavioral, comparative, certification, or portability evidence exists
out_of_scope: Whole-repository certification from a partial diff
Proof that unexecuted code is correct
acceptance_conditions: Intent and missing material context are reconstructed
Every finding explains a concrete failure mechanism
Severity and evidence levels are defensible
Duplicate or low-value findings are excluded
Ship decision follows the strongest supported finding or material unknown

specifications.purpose: Compare technical options consistently under explicit constraints, evidence, uncertainty, operational consequences, and reversibility.

required: One-sentence decision
At least two options or an explicit status-quo option
Hard constraints
Decision criteria and relative importance
optional: System, workload, team, and business context
invalid_or_blocking_states: The decision is not distinguishable from its suggested implementation
All options lack enough definition for shared comparison
Material hard constraints are unknown
input_contract.missing_information_behavior: Return HOLD and request the smallest evidence needed to resolve the most decision-relevant uncertainty.

output_contract.completion_rule: Every viable option is evaluated against the same frame; hard-constraint violations cannot be hidden by a weighted score.

constraints: Separate supplied fact, source claim, inference, and assumption
Do not invent benchmarks, pricing, limits, incidents, capabilities, or effort
Reject non-viable options before preference scoring
Expose migration, operating burden, lock-in, failure modes, and reversal cost
Do not force a winner when evidence leaves options tied
Treat numerical scores as summaries rather than evidence

expected_value.statement: Make technical trade-offs, decisive assumptions, and the next highest-information validation step visible before commitment.

known_limitations: Current pricing, vendor behavior, or product capabilities require fresh external evidence when material
Criteria weights still reflect human priorities
The prompt does not execute benchmarks or proofs of concept
No F4 behavioral, comparative, certification, or portability evidence exists
acceptance_conditions: Decision and constraints are normalized
Non-viable options are removed explicitly
Evidence, inference, assumptions, and unknowns remain distinct
Recommendation names its strongest counterargument and dependency assumptions
Reversal triggers and next validation actions are concrete

specifications.purpose: Provide a configurable operating system for repeated defect and incident diagnosis with governed evidence, safety, hypothesis, action, and confirmation policies.

required: Configured diagnostic target, consumer, authority, and primary outcome
Configured required evidence fields
Configured root-cause confirmation threshold
Configured safety and approval policy
A concrete defect or incident instance
optional: Recent deployments, dependency, configuration, data, or schema changes
Last known good point and prior incidents
invalid_or_blocking_states: Required policy placeholders remain unresolved
Required instance evidence is absent
Requested action exceeds configured authority
input_contract.missing_information_behavior: Return INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE or DIAGNOSE_FIRST and name only evidence capable of changing the diagnosis or action.

output_contract.completion_rule: Configured evidence and safety thresholds govern the strongest conclusion and every production-affecting recommendation.

constraints: Never promote INFERRED or UNKNOWN to OBSERVED
Never emit CAUSE_CONFIRMED before the configured confirmation threshold
Keep destructive, evidence-destroying, or security-disabling shortcuts forbidden
Rank bounded hypotheses by evidence and discriminating-test value
Separate diagnostic, containment, mitigation, and durable-fix actions
Expose approval requirements and production risk

expected_value.statement: Reduce diagnosis-policy drift across incidents and make the workflow reusable in tickets, runbooks, agents, and support escalation.

known_limitations: The template is not directly executable until policy placeholders are configured
A generic confirmation threshold may be inappropriate for a specific system
It cannot confer production-change authority
No F4 behavioral, comparative, certification, or portability evidence exists
out_of_scope: Bypassing incident authority or change controls
acceptance_conditions: All material configuration points are resolved
Input and diagnostic states are enforceable
Safety and approval boundaries are explicit
Hypotheses and checks remain inspectable
Verification tests both symptom resolution and mechanism consistency

specifications.purpose: Turn a recurring AI-assisted technical task into an explicit, inspectable operating contract with stable context, evidence, decision, output, verification, and fallback semantics.

required: Workflow identity, owner or consumer, and primary outcome
Configured required inputs and input validation rules
Allowed context and disallowed assumptions
Evidence threshold, operating constraints, task-specific procedure, decision policy, and output contract
optional: External research source, freshness, and citation policy
invalid_or_blocking_states: Material placeholders remain unresolved
Required input semantics contradict each other
The task-specific execution procedure is absent
The output consumer or contract is undefined
input_contract.missing_information_behavior: Return BLOCKED, NEEDS_REVIEW, or UNSUPPORTED with the smallest unblocking evidence set and any safe partial result.

output_contract.completion_rule: The configured consumer-facing output contract, rather than the template's suggested headings, defines completion.

constraints: Unconfigured sections that do not affect execution must be removed
Context outside the configured boundary remains UNKNOWN
Material claims require evidence state
The strongest conclusion must meet the configured threshold
Decision state cannot be strengthened for rhetorical decisiveness
Verification and fallback behavior must survive representation changes

expected_value.statement: Reduce workflow drift and reverse engineering by making reusable AI operating semantics explicit across prompts, forms, configs, tickets, and agent invocations.

known_limitations: Domain correctness depends on the configured task-specific procedure
The general template may be excessive for simple one-off tasks
Machine-readable representation does not guarantee semantic preservation
No F4 behavioral, comparative, certification, or portability evidence exists
out_of_scope: Simple one-off questions where governance adds no value
Granting external tool or decision authority
acceptance_conditions: Every retained section changes execution or inspection
Required and optional inputs are distinguishable
Allowed context and evidence thresholds are explicit
Decision transitions and consumer output are stable
Fallback and verification can be applied by the intended integration

specifications.purpose: Provide a configurable code-review operating system with stable review lenses, evidence and severity thresholds, ship-state transitions, output, and verification policy.

required: Configured workflow name, review target, intent, consumer, and ship authority
Code, diff, or exact changed files
Runtime or language context sufficient to interpret the change
Configured review lenses, reporting threshold, severity, and ship policy
optional: Schema, API, database, authorization, concurrency, deployment, or compatibility context
Custom review lenses and organization severity rubric
invalid_or_blocking_states: Policy placeholders remain unresolved
No reviewable change is supplied
Key context is insufficient for the configured blocking decision
input_contract.missing_information_behavior: Use INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT or REVIEW_REQUIRED and ask only for context capable of changing a finding or ship decision.

output_contract.completion_rule: Only findings meeting configured evidence and severity thresholds may affect the configured ship transition.

constraints: Enabled lenses only; disabled lenses produce no filler
Every finding connects evidence, mechanism, impact, fix, and verification
CONFIRMED, LIKELY, QUESTION, and DISMISSED semantics remain distinct
Do not invent test or runtime evidence
Reject style-only, duplicate, contradicted, or immaterial candidates
Preserve configured human or CI authority

expected_value.statement: Make code-review policy reusable across repositories and integrations while keeping findings and ship decisions inspectable.

known_limitations: The template requires explicit team policy configuration before use
Repository-wide context may be unavailable in a supplied diff
The workflow does not execute tests unless tools and authority are separately supplied
No F4 behavioral, comparative, certification, or portability evidence exists
out_of_scope: Automatic merge authority unless explicitly granted elsewhere
acceptance_conditions: Review policy fields are resolved
Input state is explicit
Every accepted finding survives challenge
Ship decision follows configured transitions
Verification plan covers applicable happy, edge, failure, security, regression, and observability paths

specifications.purpose: Provide a configurable decision system for technical choices with governed source quality, freshness, hard constraints, reversibility, transition states, and discriminating experiments.

required: Configured decision name, owner, question, options, horizon, and deadline
System and product context
Hard constraints and decision criteria
Allowed evidence sources, freshness, citation, and quality policy
Configured decision-state transitions
invalid_or_blocking_states: Material policy placeholders remain unresolved
All options violate hard constraints
Critical criteria depend only on evidence below the configured threshold
The decision owner or target decision is undefined
input_contract.missing_information_behavior: Return HOLD or REJECT_ALL and design the smallest discriminating evidence request or experiment instead of forcing a winner.

output_contract.completion_rule: Only viable options enter preference comparison, and recommendation strength cannot exceed configured evidence quality.

constraints: Hard constraints precede scoring
Every material claim keeps source, freshness, applicability, and evidence state when required
Weak evidence and assumptions remain visible
Scores do not override evidence or constraints
Second-order consequences and exit cost are considered where material
A HOLD result must propose a genuinely discriminating experiment

expected_value.statement: Make recurring technical decisions more consistent, current, reversible, and reviewable across ADR, vendor, migration, and platform workflows.

known_limitations: Fresh external facts require permitted research at execution time
Evidence-quality grades still require contextual judgment
A generic template cannot determine organization-specific criteria weights
No F4 behavioral, comparative, certification, or portability evidence exists
acceptance_conditions: All hard constraints and criteria are explicit
Source policy and freshness are enforceable
Every option has a viability state
Decision status follows configured transitions
Reversal triggers and discriminating next actions can change a future decision
